profiles.name: Civic Continuum
profiles.intro: Meet Sage, our business ambassador prototype. Ask about our work and see the evidence behind each answer.

faqs.question: What does Civic Continuum do?
faqs.answer: Civic Continuum develops prototypes and research around AI accountability, permission controls and human–AI interaction. Sage, Maya Node and Aurora are distinct projects with different stages of development.

faqs.question: What can Sage do today?
faqs.answer: Sage has a companion runtime and a separate browser device demonstrator. Camera preview, location display and speech-to-text have founder-reported tablet observations. Camera preview is not scene understanding; audible replies and full browser-to-runtime integration still have open verification gates.
faqs.sourceLabel: Sage README: demonstrated behavior and limits

faqs.question: What happens to my information here?
faqs.answer: This prototype uses typed text only. It does not request your camera, microphone or location, and sends no question to an AI provider. Chat and approval state stay in this tab's memory and clear on Stop or reload. Optional downloads are files you choose to save. Site hosting may maintain its own access logs.

faqs.question: Is a real robot connected?
faqs.answer: No robot is connected. The drawing is an illustrative browser preview of an ambassador's responses. Reachy SDK integration, MuJoCo simulation and physical-device testing have not been completed by this prototype.

faqs.question: Can I buy this service now?
faqs.answer: This is an owner-review prototype, not an operating paid service. A proposed limited pilot would need an agreed scope, a working deployment, acceptance tests and written commercial terms before payment or customer launch.

profiles.name: Harbor Cycle Studio
profiles.intro: A fictional bicycle workshop, showing how a small business could answer recurring questions without paid AI calls.

faqs.question: What are your hours?
faqs.answer: In this fictional example, the workshop opens Tuesday–Saturday, 10 AM–6 PM. These are demonstration hours, not a real business listing.

faqs.question: What repairs do you offer?
faqs.answer: The fictional workshop offers flat-tire repair, brake adjustments and basic bicycle tune-ups. E-bike batteries and electrical systems are outside this example's service scope.

faqs.question: How much is a tune-up?
aliases: how much is a tune up
how much does a tune up cost
faqs.answer: The sample price for a basic tune-up is $80, with parts and additional work quoted separately. This is a fictional demonstration price, not a live offer.
faqs.sourceLabel: Fictional owner-approved price sheet • sample v1

faqs.question: Can you book my bike in?
faqs.answer: I cannot book or contact anyone in this prototype. Choose Prepare a handoff to review and download a local draft for a person. No appointment will be created.
